columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Purpose-built to start, manage, or join online or in-person book clubs.
Core features: club creation (multiple clubs per account), digital bookshelves, meeting scheduling, polls/voting for book selection, member management, RSVPs, and messaging/chat.
Import book lists from CSV (e.g. exported Goodreads lists) to populate shelves.
Granular privacy per club: share or hide contact info and personal shelves; email notification preferences; account deletion.

strengths.title: Purpose-built infrastructure for clubs
strengths.detail: Operational pieces many clubs otherwise manage via email, spreadsheets, and group chats, selection, scheduling, reminders, RSVPs, shelves, and messaging.

strengths.title: Supports online and in-person clubs
strengths.detail: Flexible for hybrid, fully virtual, or in-person groups; one platform for logistics regardless of meeting style.

strengths.title: Easy onboarding and list import
strengths.detail: Import legacy reading lists from CSV (e.g. Goodreads exports) to quickly populate shelves and history.

strengths.title: Reasonable privacy controls
strengths.detail: Members choose what information and shelves to share with club peers, useful for mixed online/offline groups.

weaknesses.title: Not a full reading social network
weaknesses.detail: Focused on club logistics, not broader discovery, algorithmic recommendations, or a large-scale social graph like Goodreads or Fable.

weaknesses.title: Limited direct integration with ebook/audio platforms
weaknesses.detail: Tracks book choices and meetings but does not provide native reading or listening, users still rely on external apps.

weaknesses.title: Club-centric UX may feel narrow for solo readers
weaknesses.detail: Strongest when there is a group; solo readers may prefer StoryGraph, Goodreads, Literal, or Fable.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Bookclubs (Bookclubz) is free app and site to start, manage, and join book clubs, shelves, scheduling, polls, RSVPs, messaging, and CSV list import. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Bookclubs is a free app and website that make organizing a book club simple, helping you start, manage, and join clubs, schedule meetings, choose books, track reading, and chat all in one place. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Bookclubs (Bookclubz) side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Bookclubs (Bookclubz) you can use Community & Messaging as a first-class product job. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Bookclubs (Bookclubz)

You can use both. Bookclubs (Bookclubz) keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Bookclubs (Bookclubz). Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
